patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] btrfs: fix block group ref leak when scrub races with unused bg deletion

version_history.subject: [PATCH] btrfs: fix block group ref leak when scrub races with unused bg deletion

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a block group reference leak in Btrfs when scrub operations race with unused block group deletion. The issue arises from concurrent access to the `unused_bgs` list, where a block group can be added back to it after being removed. To fix this, the patch introduces a check for an empty list before taking a new reference on the block group.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: Approved the patch with a Reviewed-by tag. The fix looks correct and should prevent the reference leak issue.
review_comments.raw_body:
\u5728 2026/11/12 10:38, Boris Burkov \u5199\u9053:
> btrfs_delete_unused_bgs() takes a block group off fs_info->unused_bgs
> with list_del_init() and, when discard is on, later moves it onto the
> transaction's deleted_bgs list and takes a reference for that list
> membership. Meanwhile, it is possible for scrub to add it back to the
> unused block groups list:
> 
>           CLEANER                               SCRUB
>    btrfs_delete_unused_bgs()
>      list_del_init(&bg->bg_list)
>                                          scrub_enumerate_chunks()
>                                            btrfs_mark_bg_unused(bg)
>                                              if (list_empty(&bg->bg_list))
>                                                btrfs_get_block_group(bg)
>                                                list_add_tail(unused_bgs)
>      list_move(&bg->bg_list, deleted_bgs)
>      btrfs_get_block_group(bg)
> 
> Other users of list_move() for bg->bg_list (like btrfs_mark_bg_unused
> itself) ensure that the list was empty under the bg spin lock to decide
> whether it merits a fresh reference for being linked to the list, and
> we need to apply that pattern here as well.
> 
> Note that this is not abstracted to a helper function because some of
> the callers have additional logic deciding whether to link it or not and
> I think a twice used, twice unused helper would be more confusing than it
> would be helpful.
> 
> Reported-by: Sashiko <sashiko-bot@kernel.org>
> Link: https://sashiko.dev/#/bug/linux-821034ac-556f-4d72-af2c-d04468879af8
> Signed-off-by: Boris Burkov <boris@bur.io>

Reviewed-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>

Thanks,
Qu

>   fs/btrfs/block-group.c | 7 +++++--
>   1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
> 
> diff --git a/fs/btrfs/block-group.c b/fs/btrfs/block-group.c
> index 027830a53f7d..0b3b8843d221 100644
> --- a/fs/btrfs/block-group.c
> +++ b/fs/btrfs/block-group.c
> @@ -1830,12 +1830,15 @@ void btrfs_delete_unused_bgs(struct btrfs_fs_info *fs_info)
>   			/*
>   			 * A concurrent scrub might have added us to the list
>   			 * fs_info->unused_bgs, so use a list_move operation
> -			 * to add the block group to the deleted_bgs list.
> +			 * to add the block group to the deleted_bgs list. In
> +			 * that case the list reference moves along with it,
> +			 * so only take a new one if we were not on any list.
>   			 */
> +			if (list_empty(&block_group->bg_list))
> +				btrfs_get_block_group(block_group);
>   			list_move(&block_group->bg_list,
>   				  &trans->transaction->deleted_bgs);
>   			spin_unlock(&fs_info->unused_bgs_lock);

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 1/7] mm: support promotion-only NUMA hinting scans
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces a new NUMA hinting scan mode called 'promotion-only' that allows the kernel to focus on identifying when VMAs become active, rather than optimizing scanning activity based on heuristics like read-only VMAs or VMA activeness. The patch adds a new flag MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY and modifies various functions in the mm module to use this flag to determine the type of walk to perform. This change is necessary for memory-tiering fixes and improves the interface by keeping it focused on scan intent, rather than plumbing VMA-derived state.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 2/7] mm: allow shared folios to be promoted to a fast tier
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios mapped by multiple processes to be promoted from slow memory to a faster tier, while maintaining existing restrictions for ordinary placement and non-promotion migrations. The patch renames the `folio_use_access_time` function to `folio_numab_promotable` to better reflect its purpose in handling memory-tiering and source-tier tests. This change enables promotion of low-tier folios to top-tier memory, but prevents east-west or north-to-south migrations. The patch addresses an issue with NUMA balancing that previously rejected shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios from being promoted.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 3/7] sched/numa: scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) balancing code to scan read-only file mappings when tiering is enabled, but only performs promotion scans on these mappings. This change prevents hot file folios from being placed on slow memory in tiering mode, which can cause east-west placement bouncing. The patch also updates the walk type for each VMA (Virtual Memory Area) based on the balancing-mode snapshot taken in task_numa_work().

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 4/7] sched/numa: separate VMA placement from scan continuation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch separates the logic of VMA placement from scan continuation in the Linux kernel's NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) scheduling code. The existing `vma_is_accessed` function returns true for both placement eligibility and scan progress, which is not distinguishable by callers. This patch renames the function to `vma_needs_placement_scan`, introduces a new field in the `struct vma_numab_state` to track promotion-only scans, and updates the task's NUMA work to handle continuation state correctly. The separation allows PID-inactive VMAs to be scanned for promotion without treating scan continuation as evidence of placement eligibility.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 5/7] sched/numa: scan PID-inactive VMAs for promotion
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series enhances the vma scanning logic in the Linux kernel's scheduler to promote hot slow-tier memory by bypassing a filter that suppresses faults for inactive VMAs. The changes allow for more efficient memory tiering and reduce CXL bandwidth utilization, resulting in major throughput improvements for database workloads.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 6/7] mm: use BIT() for change_protection() flags

The current implementation uses open-coded shifts, which can be error-prone and difficult to maintain. By switching to BIT(), the code becomes more readable and easier to understand.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/4] mm: zswap: fix shrinker count for the root memcg
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a zswap shrinker count issue for the root memory cgroup (memcg). The problem arises from the fact that the root memcg's stats do not account for its own zswap entries, leading to incorrect scaling of freeable entries. To fix this, the patch uses the zswap pool-wide counters instead of the memcg's statistics, ensuring accurate counting and proper reclaiming of pages.

review_comments.author: Johannes Weiner
review_comments.summary: Provided a Reviewed-by tag without any specific comments or suggestions.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Mon, Nov 09, 2026 at 05:53:18PM -0800, Joanne Koong wrote:
> zswap_shrinker_count() scales the number of freeable entries on a
> memcg's zswap LRU by the memcg's compression ratio. That compression
> ratio is computed from the memcg's MEMCG_ZSWAP_B and MEMCG_ZSWAPPED
> stats.
> 
> However, for the root memcg, the zswap entries owned by the root memcg
> itself are never accounted for in the stats (obj_cgroup_charge_zswap()
> skips the root objcg, and before the root memcg had an objcg, its
> entries weren't charged at all). The stats only reflect the entries
> owned by the root memcg's descendants. When the root memcg's descendants
> have no zswap entries (eg when the whole workload runs in the root
> cgroup), the shrinker reports nothing to reclaim for the root memcg, and
> its zswap entries are never written back by the shrinker. When its
> descendants do have entries, the root memcg's entries are scaled by the
> descendants' compression ratio instead of a ratio that includes them.
> 
> Fix this by using the zswap pool-wide counters for the root memcg
> instead. The zswap pool-wide counters cover every zswap entry, including
> those owned by the root memcg.
> 
> This also gets rid of having to flush the root memcg's stats, which
> flushes every cgroup in the system.
> 
> In a VM running a reclaim-heavy workload in the root cgroup with the
> zswap shrinker enabled, the shrinker wrote back no pages before this
> change (zswpwb stayed at 0) and 1016 pages with it.
> 
> Fixes: b5ba474f3f51 ("zswap: shrink zswap pool based on memory pressure")
> Acked-by: Yosry Ahmed <yosry@kernel.org>
> Reviewed-by: SJ Park <sj@kernel.org>
> Acked-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>
> Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>

Reviewed-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/4] mm: memcg: read root lruvec stats from the node counters
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the way the root memory cgroup (memcg) reads its LRU vector statistics from node counters. For most stats, it directly reads from the node counter to avoid flushing the entire system, which is expensive. However, for certain kernel memory stats and hugetlb, it still needs to read the rstat value because their node counters also count unaccounted memory. This change improves accuracy of root memcg statistics and reduces flush overhead.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/4] mm: workingset: skip the root memcg flush in workingset_test_recent()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the workingset_test_recent() function to skip flushing the root memory cgroup's statistics when it is not necessary. The function now checks if the eviction memory cgroup is the root cgroup before deciding whether to flush its statistics. This optimization reduces the time taken for a root flush from 69us on an 80-CPU machine with little activity, and 0.9ms with high activity, down to negligible time. The patch also notes that flushing is still necessary for reclaim operations, but this change improves performance on systems with many memory cgroups.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/4] mm/damon/core: use node counters instead of flushing the root memcg
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the DAMON core to use node counters instead of flushing the root memory cgroup (memcg) statistics when calculating LRU sizes for the goal's memcg on its node. This change improves performance by reducing the frequency of flush operations, which were previously unratelimited and occurred every time the goal was evaluated. The patch achieves this by leveraging a new function in lruvec_page_state() that directly reads the root memcg's LRU sizes from the node counters.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series proposes to read root memcg stats from global counters instead of flushing, which is expensive and can lead to stale statistics. The patches aim to optimize the behavior for the root cgroup by allowing direct access to global counters, reducing the need for flushing and improving performance.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v1] mm/rmap: fix migration entries being treated as partial unmaps

version_history.subject: [PATCH v1] mm/rmap: fix migration entries being treated as partial unmaps

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes an issue where migration entries in the Linux kernel are being treated as partial unmaps, leading to incorrect behavior such as unnecessary folio splits and overcounting of split_deferred statistics. The problem occurs when a large anonymous folio is migrated or split, causing the PG_partially_mapped flag to be set even though no actual unmapping has taken place. To fix this, the patch introduces a new flag that prevents __folio_remove_rmap() from marking a folio as partially mapped when migration entries are replaced for PTEs. This ensures that only actual unmappings trigger the deferred split queue and corrects the statistics. The patch also addresses issues related to migrated folios being queued for unnecessary splits and overcounting of split_deferred statistics.

review_comments.author: David (Arm)
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch addresses a similar issue he raised last year, where THPs were being incorrectly marked as partially mapped after migration or splitting, and suggested that the current patch's solution is an improvement because it copies the state to the new folio, allowing for correct splitting.

Reviewer David noted that the patch does not address all possible scenarios and asked if the issue also occurs when using try_to_unmap(), pointing out a potential oversight.

Reviewer David (Arm) expressed strong disagreement with the patch's approach, suggesting that instead of adding a 'magical boolean parameter', the rmap flags should be passed directly for another purpose. He also pointed out that the issue can be resolved by batching unmap operations in the common case and checking for partial mapping in the deferred split handler.
review_comments.raw_body:
This is a similar problem I raised in last year's LSF/MM:

https://share.daveh.de/s/bQsDpD7xigJ6wD8/download?path=&files=LSF_MM%2726_+Deferred_folio_splitting.pdf

"
2. THPs erroneously detected as partially-mapped
 * Failing migration/split/eviction after stepwise unmap
 * Remapping the folio will not fix this up
"

The news here is that we now copy the state to the new folio and can
consequently split the new folio.

---

Don't we have the same problem for try_to_unmap() in some remaining cases?

See below.

---

We will not add such magical boolean parameters. I have a patch to just pass the
rmap flags for a different purpose.

But the whole thing is rather ugly ...


You should probably look at

commit 354dffd29575cdf13154e8fb787322354aa9efc4
Author: Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Feb 14 22:30:14 2025 +1300

    mm: support batched unmap for lazyfree large folios during reclamation

    Currently, the PTEs and rmap of a large folio are removed one at a time.
    This is not only slow but also causes the large folio to be unnecessarily
    added to deferred_split, which can lead to races between the
    deferred_split shrinker callback and memory reclamation.  This patch
    releases all PTEs and rmap entries in a batch.  Currently, it only handles
    lazyfree large folios.

Batching resolves the problem in the common case. For the remaining parts, we
should likely just check in the deferred split handler whether actually
partially mapped to then clear the flag if not.

-- 
Cheers,

David

review_comments.raw_body:
On Tue, Nov 10, 2026 at 3:49 AM David Hildenbrand (Arm)
<david@kernel.org> wrote:

---

As I understand it, there's no simple way to check if a folio is
partially mapped or not under CONFIG_NO_PAGE_MAPCOUNT without doing a
rmap walk. Would it make sense to do something simpler here instead
where we just check the folio's partially mapped flag and cache that
before we replace the PTEs with migration entries, and then for those
edge cases that the batching solution doesn't cover, just restore that
flag back to its original state?

I think this would add coverage for the migration and reclaim paths,
instead of just the deferred split shrinker, but would miss the race
where someone tries to do a partial unmap while the folio has the
migration PTEs, but I think this is already a race that exists in the
batching case. imo it seems acceptable though given that the race is
pretty rare and doesn't have any adverse effects except delaying
freeing the unmapped pages until the whole folio gets unmapped.

Do you think something like this makes sense, or would you prefer
having the check in the deferred split handler?

Thanks,
Joanne

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/4] mm/huge_memory: scale thp_underused() to the folio size
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the thp_underused() function to be aware of the size of a folio, rather than just PMD-sized folios. It scales the khugepaged_max_ptes_none threshold proportionally to the number of pages in the folio, ensuring that the same fraction of zero-filled pages is tolerated for any folio size. This change will prevent issues when collapsing mTHP orders and splitting folios. The patch has no functional changes for PMD-sized folios, as their nr_pages value remains HPAGE_PMD_NR.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/4] mm/huge_memory: don't queue folios when underused splitting is inactive
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's huge memory management to prevent anonymous PMD-sized folios from being queued for underused splitting when the system is configured to tolerate any number of zero-filled pages. This change is made by factoring out a check into a new function, thp_underused_never(), which is used in both deferred_split_folio() and thp_underused(). The patch also addresses an issue where folios that were already scanned are not requeued when the sysctl changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 3/4] mm/huge_memory: add a per-order counter for underused splits
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-order counter for underused huge page splits in the Linux kernel's memory management system. The existing thp_underused_split_page counter only counts PMD-sized folios, but this change introduces a new split_underused stat that tracks underused splits of all sizes. This is done to match the behavior of other THP split stats and provide more accurate information about huge page usage. The patch makes changes to several files, including Documentation/admin-guide/mm/transhuge.rst, include/linux/huge_mm.h, and mm/huge_memory.c.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 4/4] mm: add anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series adds anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list, addressing a memory regression issue on arm64 systems with 2M THP=always configuration. The change mirrors what is already done for PMD-sized folios and ensures that fully mapped mTHP folios can be split by the deferred split shrinker when under memory pressure.

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary: Barry agreed with the hardcoded 2MB minimum size for mTHP folios to be queued for underused splitting, which was previously discussed and decided upon.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 5:20 AM Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Unlike for PMD-sized folios, an anonymous mTHP folio doesn't get added
> to the deferred split list at fault or collapse time. As a result, a
> fully mapped mTHP folio that is mostly zero-filled doesn't get split by
> the deferred split shrinker when the system is under memory pressure.
>
> At Meta we would like to deploy 2M THP=always on arm64 with 64k base
> pages, as 2M gives the contpte benefits while the PMD size (512M) is too
> big to use. Without underused splitting this causes memory regressions,
> as the unused parts of those folios can never be broken down and
> reclaimed.
>
> Add anonymous mTHP folios to the deferred split list from
> map_anon_folio_pte_nopf(), mirroring what map_anon_folio_pmd_nopf()
> already does for PMD-sized folios. This covers both the fault path and
> the khugepaged mTHP collapse path. If there is memory pressure, a
> zero-filled mTHP can then be split with its zero pages remapped to the
> shared zero page and reclaimed.
>
> Only queue mTHP folios of at least 2M for underused splitting. With
> thp_underused() scaling khugepaged/max_ptes_none to the folio size, any
> folio of order 2 or above could in principle be underused, but for small
> folios it is unlikely to be worth it. An order-2 folio on 4k base pages
> can free at most four pages and on systems that only enable small mTHP
> sizes (eg Android's order-2-only configuration) zero-filled subpages
> tend to be few and short-lived.
>
> The minimum is hard-coded rather than a knob, since admins have no good
> way of choosing it, and is a size rather than an order since what a
> split recovers depends on the folio's size in bytes, and the same order
> means very different sizes across different base page sizes. It can be
> lowered later if data shows smaller sizes are worth it. PMD-sized folios
> are exempt from the minimum in order to maintain backwards compatibility
> since on some architectures (s390, with a 1M PMD) the PMD size can be
> below 2M.
>
> To minimize overhead on the common order-0 fault path, the
> deferred_split_folio() call is guarded by an inline folio_test_large()
> check.
>
> Suggested-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
> Signed-off-by: Joanne Koong <joannelkoong@gmail.com>
> ---

I believe we discussed this before and agreed that a
hardcoded 2MB would be a better starting point.

Reviewed-by: Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org>

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses memory regressions caused by 2M THP=always on arm64 by allowing the underused shrinker to handle anonymous mTHP folios. Finally, it queues anonymous mTHP folios on the deferred split list with a minimum size of 2M.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of get_page_from_freelist() to only skip nodes with kswapd running if they are below their relevant low-memory watermark. This change addresses a problem where high-order allocation failures would wake up kswapd and direct order-0 allocations to the fallback path, even when there is free space on the node. The patch was tested on 2-NUMA Meta production workloads and showed improved performance by reducing unnecessary pressure on remote nodes. The change only affects nodes that are under their low-memory watermark, ensuring that kswapd is not unnecessarily woken up.
